A regular hexagon can be divided into six equilateral triangles by drawing lines from the center to each vertex. In a regular hexagon, these triangles are equilateral, meaning all three sides of each triangle are equal. One side of the triangle is a side of the hexagon, and the other two are radii of the hexagon. Since the triangle is equilateral, the side length of the hexagon equals the side length of the triangle.

The perimeter of one equilateral triangle is 21 inches, so each side is \(21 \div 3 = 7\) inches. Therefore, each side of the regular hexagon is 7 inches. A regular hexagon has 6 sides, so its perimeter is \(6 \times 7 = 42\) inches.

Answer: 42
